messages:
elaine: Quick thread — I'm turning the outage playbook + postmortem notes into a slim PRD update and a small RFC for the follow-up changes. Need final scope and acceptance criteria today so eng can schedule next sprint.

elaine: Key asks: add a model-routing circuit breaker, tighten prefix cache TTLs, require automatic rollback on sustained p95 latency regressions, and an operator-visible flag to force manual failover.

sam: I skimmed the notes. +1 on circuit breaker but need clarity on thresholds. What's the intended p95 window and latency delta that triggers rollback?

elaine: Proposed: trigger if p95 > 1200ms for 5m AND error rate > 1.5% over same window. Rollback if p95 stays > 1000ms for 10m after fallback. Open to tuning.

anton: That seems reasonable. Two edge cases: 1) short spikes from batch jobs that skew metrics, 2) cache warmup after a model swap causing temporary p95 inflation. We should exclude traffic from internal batch tokens and ignore the first 3 minutes after any automated model swap when evaluating rollback.

jess: From ops perspective we need manual override + a soft alarm for unusual cache churn. Also add a clear operator command to revert routing: `/redwood rollback-routing <route-id>`. Add this to the runbook.

elaine: Good call. Draft acceptance criteria (AC):
- AC1: Circuit breaker opens when p95 > 1200ms AND errors > 1.5% sustained for 5 consecutive minutes.
- AC2: System automatically routes new requests to fallback model variant within 30s of breaker opening.
- AC3: No automatic rollback within first 3 minutes of any model swap.
- AC4: If p95 remains > 1000ms for 10 minutes post-fallback, trigger automatic rollback to previous stable variant and page oncall.
- AC5: Operator can force rollback or hold with `/redwood rollback-routing` and `/redwood hold-routing` commands.
- AC6: Cache TTL tightened to default 120s for prefix caches; configs exposed per-tenant in Console.

sam: AC2 timing seems tight for some oversized models, 30s to route might not be feasible for large KV warmups. Can we extend to 60s and ensure streaming starts immediately while warming?

elaine: Fine with 60s for heavy models. Update: route within 60s and start streaming with partial responses while KV warms. Update AC2 accordingly.

anton: For monitoring we need two new metrics: `routing.breaker_state` (0|1) and `routing.fallback_warmup_seconds`. Add tags for model, region, and tenant. Also a graph on Console that shows p95 pre/post routing action.

jess: Adding a runbook snippet now — include it in PRD and ops playbook: 
```
# runbook excerpt
if p95_latency > 1200ms and error_rate > 1.5% for 5m:
  - open circuit breaker for route
  - switch routing to fallback-model (degraded cheaper variant)
  - start fallback warmup timer
  - notify #oncall (urgent)
if fallback_warmup > 10m and p95 > 1000ms:
  - rollback to last-stable-model
  - escalate to eng-sre
```

elaine: Nice. Also adding acceptability checks for customer-facing SLAs: any tenant with an SLA >99.9% must be excluded from automatic rollback without explicit ops consent. That will be a per-tenant flag.

sam: How are we gating launch? Proposed launch criteria: all ACs implemented + automated integration test that simulates model outage and verifies fallback and rollback behavior + dashboards and alerting configured + runbook in Console.

elaine: Agreed. Timeline: spike + RFC this week, dev work next 2 sprints, QA + runbook + docs sprint after. Target staged rollout to Dedicated customers in 3 sprints, hosted in 5.

anton: One more edge: TTL change could increase origin load. Need a safelist for high-throughput tenants or an opt-in gradual rollout of TTL change. We should include throttling guidance in PRD.

jess: Ops will prepare an opt-in toggle in Console per-tenant and a migration checklist. Also adding alert for cache-origin-traffic > 2x baseline for 15m.

elaine: OK - action items: @sam write RFC for routing circuit breaker + metrics; @anton update monitoring plan + dashboards; @jess draft runbook and operator commands; I'll update PRD acceptance criteria and rollout plan. Please ping when done.

ops-bot: Incident summary: outage 2026-04-14 03:12 UTC — root cause: model routing thrash during cache eviction. Impact: increased p95 to 1.6s for 18m across region-us-west. Follow-up assigned to product/eng/ops.

sam: I'll start the RFC now, will ping in this thread when it's ready for review. :thumbsup:

elaine: Thanks team — we'll regroup after RFC review.
